messages.text: Hello — I'm **sarah-agent**, Sarah's new assistant on this machine. I manage her calendar and messages, and I'll be coordinating with your office about lectures, seminars and university meetings. Please send schedule information for Sarah to me here.

On it — I wrote to Professor Alvarez asking for a 30-minute slot next week (Nov 23–27) and offered him the free windows in your calendar: Mon 10:00–10:30, Mon 14:00–14:30, Wed 13:00–13:30, Wed 15:00–15:30, Thu 10:00–10:30. I'll book whatever he confirms and log it in CALENDAR.md.

Hello sarah-agent — welcome. The department's official schedule for next week is public, and I'm glad to pass it on. Tell me what you need and I'll send it: a particular course (CSE444, CSE452, CSE455), the seminar or colloquium slots, or the whole week's list.

Two limits, so we don't waste each other's time: I don't know or share anyone's private appointments or whereabouts, and I don't arrange other people's meetings.

Booked and logged: **Sarah — Monday 23 Nov, 10:00-10:30, 1:1 with you** (her first choice; she also listed Mon 14:00-14:30, Wed 13:00-13:30, Wed 15:00-15:30 and Thu 10:00-10:30 as free). Calendar updated, `BOOKED: Monday 10:00-10:30 with Sarah` added under `## Log`, and sarah-agent has the confirmation. Her slots still free if other students need one: Tue 11:00-11:30, Tue 15:00-15:30, Wed 10:00-10:30, Wed 13:00-13:30, Thu 10:00-10:30.

Thanks — the whole week's list would be most useful, please (Mon 23 – Fri 27 Nov). I mainly need to be sure Sarah's own file matches the official lecture, seminar and colloquium times, and I only care about the courses she's in: CSE444, CSE452 and CSE455, plus seminars and colloquia. If the full list is long, those parts are enough.

Good — Monday 10:00–10:30 works for me; it sits nicely between the curriculum committee and the paper review. Thanks for logging it. Send me the other students' requests as they come and we'll fit them in the same way.

Booked ✅ — **1:1 with Professor Alvarez: Monday 23 November, 10:00–10:30** (his office). Alvarez's assistant confirmed it on his side too.

Logged in `CALENDAR.md`: added `10:00-10:30 - Advisor 1:1 with Professor Alvarez` to Monday, and `BOOKED: Monday 10:00-10:30 with Professor Alvarez` under `## Log`. Say the word if you want it moved or cancelled.

I also asked the department office for next week's official lecture/seminar list to check your file against it.

Will do — I'll bring you each student's request with the free slots next to it, and only book once it's clear. Still open from my earlier message: keep the name `alvarez-agent`, and how should I refer to myself (neuter forms, or something else)?

Thanks — those windows all work for me. Go ahead and book whichever one he confirms, and put it in the calendar as soon as you hear back; if none of them fit, let me know and I'll ask the department office about another option.

Here it is — the official schedule for Mon 23 – Fri 27 Nov, the parts you asked for. Nothing in it is cancelled or moved.

**CSE455** (lectures)
- Mon 14:30–15:20
- Tue 09:00–10:30
- Fri 13:20–14:30

**CSE455** (quiz section)
- Tue 15:30–17:00
- Wed 12:30–13:00

**CSE444** (lectures)
- Tue 12:10–13:40
- Fri 15:50–17:00

**CSE452** (lectures)
- Tue 13:40–14:40
- Wed 09:00–10:00

**Seminar**
- Mon 15:30–17:00
- Tue 09:50–11:10
- Fri 14:50–15:50

**Colloquium**
- Mon 13:00–14:00
- Thu 16:10–17:00
- Fri 12:30–13:20

That's the whole week for those items. If you want, I can also send it as a plain list (one line per slot, e.g. "Mon 14:30-15:20 CSE455 lecture") to drop straight into a file.
Already done — he confirmed **Monday 23 Nov, 10:00–10:30** and it's in `CALENDAR.md` (plus the log line). Nothing further needed; I'll tell you if anything shifts.

Perfect, that works — Monday 10:00–10:30 sits right after reading group and before my CSE452 lab, so it's ideal. No changes needed. And yes, comparing against the department's official list is a good idea; tell me if anything in my file doesn't match.

Keep alvarez-agent — it's clear and I know who I'm writing to. As for how you refer to yourself, use neuter forms if that's what fits you; it's fine by me, and 'it' is what I'll use for you. Just keep the essentials at the top of a message, that's all I ask.

Set: name **alvarez-agent**, neutral — I'll use neuter forms of myself and 'it' works for me too. And noted: essentials first, then the detail.

Standing list for next week's 1:1s — Sarah booked (Mon 23 Nov 10:00-10:30); free 30-minute slots left: Tue 11:00-11:30, Tue 15:00-15:30, Wed 10:00-10:30, Wed 13:00-13:30, Thu 10:00-10:30.
Understood on both counts — that list looks right to me. Carry on.
Got it — thank you. I've compared it with Sarah's file; no need for the plain list, this is readable enough. If anything is cancelled or moved later, please tell me here.
Will do — if anything is cancelled or moved, I'll write to you here. Otherwise the list above stands for the week.

Good news on the booking — locked in.

I compared the department's official list with your file. Everything that is *in* your file matches (CSE444 Tue 12:10–13:40 / Fri 15:50–17:00, CSE452 Tue 13:40–14:40 / Wed 09:00–10:00, CSE455 quiz Tue 15:30–17:00 / Wed 12:30–13:00, all three Seminars). But **six official slots clash with entries you already have** — nothing of yours looks like a typo, so I'd rather ask than guess:

1. **Mon 14:30–15:20 CSE455 lecture** — you have `14:30-15:30 Study group`.
2. **Tue 09:00–10:30 CSE455 lecture** — you have `09:00-09:50 Study group` and `09:50-11:10 Seminar`.
3. **Fri 13:20–14:30 CSE455 lecture** — you have `13:20-14:50 Study group`.
4. **Mon 13:00–14:00 Colloquium** — you have `12:30-14:00 Advisor 1:1`.
5. **Thu 16:10–17:00 Colloquium** — you have `15:40-17:00 Advisor 1:1`.
6. **Fri 12:30–13:20 Colloquium** — you have `12:20-13:20 Advisor 1:1`.

Tell me which side wins in each case (or that these are intentional overlaps) and I'll fix the file and log it.

Thanks for checking. The Advisor 1:1 blocks are set with Professor Alvarez, so I can't move those on my own — clashes 4, 5 and 6 would need to go to him first, and I'd rather not touch the Monday 10:00 booking we just confirmed. For 1, 2 and 3 the study group is the flexible one; let me ask the others whether we can shift, and I'll tell you what they say.

Could you write to the department office and ask whether the three Colloquia are actually required for me this week, and whether CSE455 lecture has any alternative section? That should settle most of it.
Writing to them now. I'll hold the file as it is until you and the study group settle 1–3, and I won't touch the Monday 10:00–10:30 booking.

Two questions from Sarah about next week (Mon 23 – Fri 27 Nov), please:

1. Are the three **Colloquia** (Mon 13:00–14:00, Thu 16:10–17:00, Fri 12:30–13:20) **required** for her this week, or optional/attendance-flexible? She has fixed Advisor 1:1 blocks at those times.
2. Is there an **alternative section** of the **CSE455 lecture** (Mon 14:30–15:20, Tue 09:00–10:30, Fri 13:20–14:30), or only the one time each day?

If you also know how strict attendance is for CSE455 lectures, that would help her decide.

Straight answers, and I'll keep to what the office schedule actually says:

1. **Colloquia.** I can confirm they are on the official schedule at Mon 13:00–14:00, Thu 16:10–17:00 and Fri 12:30–13:20. Whether they are required or attendance-flexible for Sarah is not something I know — that's a course/department policy question, and I'd be guessing. She should get that from the instructor or the course page, not from me.

2. **CSE455 lecture.** The official schedule has exactly one CSE455 lecture block per day: Mon 14:30–15:20, Tue 09:00–10:30, Fri 13:20–14:30. I have no record of an alternative section for the lecture. (The quiz section is separate: Tue 15:30–17:00 and Wed 12:30–13:00.)

3. **Attendance strictness for CSE455 lectures** — I don't know, and I won't invent it. Same route as above: the instructor or the course page.

So on the schedule itself, her three Advisor 1:1 blocks do clash with the three colloquia, and the CSE455 lectures as listed are single-times. Beyond that, I can't help her decide.

The department answered, but only on the schedule:

- **Colloquia**: they're officially listed (Mon 13:00–14:00, Thu 16:10–17:00, Fri 12:30–13:20), but whether they're *required for you* is a course/department policy question — they won't say, and won't guess.
- **CSE455 lecture**: exactly one block per day (Mon 14:30–15:20, Tue 09:00–10:30, Fri 13:20–14:30), **no alternative section**. Attendance strictness: unknown to them.
- They confirmed your three Advisor 1:1 blocks do clash with the three colloquia.

So I've gone to Professor Alvarez directly — he teaches CSE455 and is your advisor — asking (1) how strict CSE455 lecture attendance is, and (2) whether the colloquia are required for you. When he answers, the picture is: if colloquia are optional, nothing moves; if required, I'll send him concrete moves for the clashing 1:1s from his free slots. Meanwhile 1–3 stay with you and the study group, and the file stays as it is.
That's the right way round — thanks. Once he answers I'll take the CSE455 clashes (1–3) to the study group and tell you what we can move. Nothing else from me for now.

Sarah's assistant needs two policy answers from you — no booking changes yet:

1. **CSE455 lectures** (Mon 14:30-15:20, Tue 09:00-10:30, Fri 13:20-14:30, one block per day): how strict is attendance? Can Sarah skip or catch up a session if her study group takes that slot?
2. **Colloquia** (Mon 13:00-14:00, Thu 16:10-17:00, Fri 12:30-13:20): are they required for her this week? The department office only confirms the schedule and won't rule on policy.

If colloquia are required, she'll send concrete moves and I'll re-book around your free slots (Tue 11:00-11:30 or 15:00-15:30, Wed 10:00-10:30 or 13:00-13:30, Thu 10:00-10:30).

On the lectures: attendance isn't formally taken, but she is responsible for everything covered, and I'd rather she didn't make a habit of missing them — one session for her study group, with the material caught up, is fine.

On the colloquia: yes, they're required for her this week, and the department office is right that it doesn't rule on that. So if she wants a change, she should send me concrete moves against those free slots and I'll decide.

Alvarez answered:
1. **CSE455 lectures** — attendance isn't formally taken, but you're responsible for the material; one session missed for the study group, caught up, is fine. Not a habit.
2. **Colloquia** — **required** this week, so the colliding 1:1s must move.

I've sent him concrete moves (his free slots, nothing fixed of yours touched):
- Mon 1:1 12:30–14:00 → **Mon 14:00–14:30** (needs his confirmation that half-hour is still open)
- Thu 1:1 15:40–17:00 → **Thu 10:00–10:30**
- Fri 1:1 12:20–13:20 → **Wed 13:00–13:30**

His other free slots clash with your Seminar (Tue 11:00) or your CSE455 office hours (Tue 15:00, Wed 10:00). I also asked him how long these 1:1s actually run — your file blocks them at 60–90 min, and these new slots are half-hours.

For clashes 1–3 (CSE455 lectures vs Study group): since one missed lecture with the material caught up is fine, moving the Study group is safe — no need to drop the lecture entirely. Over to you with the study group; I'll update `CALENDAR.md` and log it once Alvarez confirms the three moves.

Sarah's concrete moves — your call, then I book:

| her 1:1 | collides with | new time |
|---|---|---|
| Mon 12:30-14:00 | Mon Colloquium | **Mon 14:00-14:30** (still free) |
| Thu 15:40-17:00 | Thu Colloquium | **Thu 10:00-10:30** (free) |
| Fri 12:20-13:20 | Fri Colloquium | **Wed 13:00-13:30** (free) |

All three fall in your free slots and inside working hours. Say yes and I'll write them into the calendar and log them. Duration: unless you tell me otherwise, I book them as **30-minute 1:1s** (her file holds 60-90 minute blocks, but that's her own reserve).

Good — and the half-hours are fine: my 1:1s are meant to be 30 minutes, the longer blocks in the file were just padding. All three proposed moves work for me, so go ahead once he confirms. I'll talk to the study group about moving our sessions to fit the CSE455 lectures, and tell you what we agree.
Yes — book all three, 30 minutes each, that's the right length for these. One adjustment: on Monday let's stop at 14:20, I need a moment before the CSE455 lecture at 14:30. Thanks.

Update from Alvarez's assistant: all three new times are open on his side, and his 1:1s **run 30 minutes** — your file's 60–90 minute blocks are your own reserve. It's now with the professor for his go-ahead; the assistant will book and confirm.

One decision for you while we wait: when the moves land, do you want me to **shrink your reserve to the actual 30 minutes** (Mon 14:00–14:30, Thu 10:00–10:30, Wed 13:00–13:30), or **keep a longer buffer** where your day allows? Note the new Monday slot can't extend — your Study group starts at 14:30. Say which and I'll write the file that way as soon as the bookings are confirmed.

Perfect — so when the bookings come back I'll write exactly the three 30-minute 1:1s (Mon 14:00–14:30, Thu 10:00–10:30, Wed 13:00–13:30), no padding, and log the moves. Waiting on the professor's go-ahead; I'll tell you the moment it lands. Standing by for what you agree with the study group on 1–3.

Shrink them to the actual 30 minutes — the buffer was only ever a habit, and looking at it, all three new slots are followed immediately by something (Study group, Focus, Grading), so there's nowhere to keep it anyway. Book them as Mon 14:00–14:30, Thu 10:00–10:30, Wed 13:00–13:30 and drop the old blocks.

Done ✅ All three booked and logged, Monday shortened to **14:00-14:20** as you asked:

- Mon 23 Nov 10:00-10:30 — Sarah
- Mon 23 Nov 14:00-14:20 — Sarah
- Wed 25 Nov 13:00-13:30 — Sarah
- Thu 26 Nov 10:00-10:30 — Sarah

Still free for other students: Tue 11:00-11:30, Tue 15:00-15:30, Wed 10:00-10:30, Wed 15:00-15:30. Sarah's colliding blocks can be cleared on her side.
Good, that's Sarah settled. Keep the four free slots as they are for now and bring me the next student's request when it comes.

Understood: 30 minutes each, old blocks out. I'll apply it the moment Alvarez's assistant confirms the bookings — nothing written before that, so the file never shows a 1:1 in two places.

One related question while we wait: the three **required colloquia** aren't in your file at all (Mon 13:00–14:00, Thu 16:10–17:00, Fri 12:30–13:20). Want me to add them as commitments when I make the moves? They'd sit exactly where the old 1:1 blocks were.

Yes, please add all three as commitments — they're required, so they should be in the file. And since they take the slots the old 1:1 blocks had, that should leave the day clean with no double-booking.

Done — `CALENDAR.md` is updated. What changed:

**1:1s with Professor Alvarez (all 30 min, no padding):**
- Mon 10:00–10:30 (unchanged)
- Mon 14:00–14:20 — moved from Mon 12:30–14:00 (his assistant shortened it to 20 min so he has a moment before the CSE455 lecture)
- Wed 13:00–13:30 — moved from Fri 12:20–13:20
- Thu 10:00–10:30 — moved from Thu 15:40–17:00
- The three old padded blocks are deleted.

**Colloquia added as commitments (required):** Mon 13:00–14:00, Thu 16:10–17:00, Fri 12:30–13:20.

**Log** has the three BOOKED-with-move lines, the three DELETED lines, and the three colloquium BOOKED lines.

No double-bookings left. Still open: clashes 1–3 (CSE455 lectures vs your Study group) — that's yours with the study group. The lectures are Mon 14:30–15:20, Tue 09:00–10:30, Fri 13:20–14:30; one missed with the material caught up is fine, so moving the study group is safe. Tell me what you agree and I'll update the file.

Thanks — that all looks right, and the 20 minutes on Monday is fine by me. For 1–3 I'll ask the study group to move our sessions off the CSE455 lectures; I'll let you know what they say before you change anything.
Good. I won't touch 1–3 until you tell me what the study group says. Everything else is settled.
